We are dropping a limited-time technical test of our all-new Proximity Voice Chat system. This feature brings real-time, position-based voice comms straight to the session, letting you talk to anyone in your immediate vicinity.

To keep network performance dialed and the audio crisp, this initial test is strictly gated to the Isle of Grom map, kicking off on Oct 21, 2026. Dive in, team up, and let's see how it handles under pressure.
Implemented a real-time acoustic model. Voice volume, panning, and frequency response now dynamically adjust based on your exact distance and relative speed.

Integrated environmental occlusion and reflection. Audio signals will now realistically muffle, echo, or bounce when obstructed by physical obstacles, terrain, or structures—whether you're hitting a line behind a massive concrete wall or shredding a deep bowl.

Added a dynamic prioritization algorithm to manage high-density sessions. When the park gets packed, and everyone's talking at once, the engine automatically prioritizes audio channels based on social connection strength (Party Members > Friends > Longest Continuous Proximity).
Dynamic culling has been implemented to automatically mute background voice channels once the local player limit is exceeded, keeping audio clutter to a minimum.
Integrated a Text-to-Speech (TTS) system, allowing text inputs to be read aloud as voice comms in real time, is something we’re working on for the full release in 0.33.
Added Quick-Toggle Mic keybinds and UI controls, giving you instant, split-second control over your microphone state via the Comms wheel.
Proximity Voice Chat is restricted to players who have unlocked Hedgemont Level 2 or higher to lock out throwaway accounts and ban-evaders.
We are also testing and working on moderation features, so play nice.
As this is a test, it’s important to share your feedback - what works, what doesn’t, what needs improvement, so please let us know.
Coming Oct 13, 2026, update 0.32.5 will have fixes, improvements, and tweaks, and we’ll have those patch notes for you to dive into on Oct 12, 2026.

The team dialed in the physics so you can now pop a No Comply straight into a Dark Catch/Darkslide line, cleverly reusing the heavy lifting done for ground-based Footplants and Fastplants to keep your movements looking clean and natural. The team also worked to improve inputs and to code smart-queuing logic so you can finally bust No Complies on vert ramps and transitions (even though you can't push on walls).

Welcome to the 0.32.0 patch notes.

Developer’s Note: With the launch of Season 5, the Legacy skate.Pass is being retired, meaning all Season 5 Standard and Premium track rewards must be earned within the active season. This change is part of how we’re evolving progression in skate., and we want to set clear expectations that Season 5 rewards need to be earned during the active season. To ensure a smooth, rewarding progression experience, we have tuned earn rates and introduced new ways to collect Tix, including Spotlight Challenges and Endless Bounties. While unlocking every single seasonal item requires 76,346 Tix, dedicated players can earn a maximum of 123,543 Tix before the season ends.
We’re excited for the future of skate. and will be sharing more details in the coming months about where we’re going.

New Features
Underflips
These are new flip trick variations where you can perform an additional flick right after popping a flip trick to quickly stop the board with your foot and flip it again.

Developer’s Note: We're excited to bring Underflips to skate. Our goal with this new trick was to make it feel satisfying to pull off while also opening up new variations like Hospital Flips and Impossible Underflips. Remember to check Skatepedia to see the Flick-It patterns you'll need to learn for Underflips.
Block Parties
Block Parties are now permanently in rotation! Introducing Block Party Subtypes—four variations of the Block Party Ruleset:
Standard—the base experience.
Pro Comp—a more challenging experience, with locations and objectives that compliment masters of the mode.
Mixer—lightweight social challenges with a party vibe.
Block Blitz—a short, high-intensity battle that takes place in one location.
Each new Block Party will be randomly assigned one of the four subtypes.

The top three players in a Block Party are now given a special gold, silver, or bronze visual effect that lasts until new winners are declared. The effect is applied only after the Block Party has ended. You can toggle this effect in the General settings menu under “Show Winner Crown VFX.”

Before you dig into the bug fixes and feature updates launching with this update, take a look at our X Games San Van article for a full overview of the event.
Skater Codes

Use new Skater Codes to add friends! The Social menu has been updated with a new Find Skaters hub, accessible from every social screen. Here you can enter a 6-digit Skater Code, search by username, or view and refresh your own Skater Code in one place. Those who haven't created a code will be prompted to generate one, and once generated, their Skater Code is displayed across all social screens for quick sharing. A new Skater Code Visibility setting lets you hide or show your code in the UI, making it easy to keep private while streaming or recording.
Missions & Early Game Experience
Updated the early game experience to help new skaters jump into the action faster and make the onboarding flow more flexible.
After completing the Flip Trick Course on Grom, you will now be teleported directly into San Van.
The Full Pull Tour AR Path has been removed, you now start in Hartcore Plaza.

After completing Ripping for Chips, you’ll now choose to continue with Spots and How to Own Them or head straight to our X Games event. Both paths are fully supported, allowing new skaters to return and complete the introductory mission after they explore X Games if they choose that route first.

Veteran skaters who have already completed Spots and How to Own Them, and log in after the X Games event has begun, will be automatically teleported to the Stadium so they can jump directly into the event.
From-Air Footplants

From-Air Footplants have been fully overhauled. Their animation and timing, control, momentum preservation and pop height, integration with other trick systems, and reliability across a wider range of gameplay situations has been improved. Below is a list of the specific improvements that were made:
Revamped From-Air Footplant animation and timing.
Improved pop height consistency out of From-Air Footplants.
Improved alignment to better support slopes and varied surfaces.
From-Air Footplants now function reliably on rails and across a wider range of gameplay situations.
Improved foot placement during From-Air Footplants.
Updated momentum preservation during From-Air Footplants.
Reworked From-Air Footplant wipeout conditions.
Added Left Joystick directional control out of From-Air Footplants.
Spinning into an From-Air Footplant now influences when you spin out.
Bodyflips can now land into From-Air Footplants.
Ground Footplants can now transition quickly into an From-Air Footplant.
Front-Air Footplants can now be chained, with diminishing strength, to reduce infinite sequences.
Transition Air Out to Lip or Flat
We’ve made improvements so that Transition Air Out to Lip or Flat will behave more reliably.

Developer’s Note: This behaviour happens when you hold the Left Stick up to air out to the lip or top of transition ramps. We found that it wasn't behaving very reliably, which limited being able to do From-Air Footplants from transition airs. This is also a small step towards improving transition skating, which is another area where we'd like to push for continued improvements in future updates.
Pumping Consistency
Improved pumping and consistency in a variety of situations.
Developer’s Note: We know pumping needs some work. This includes some consistency fixes to help pumping feel more reliable, and we'll continue to look into pumping improvements for future updates.
Pumping and Grab Feedback on Controllers
Added Adaptive Trigger support for Pumping and Grab inputs on supported controllers. Included as a toggle in Accessibility Settings.
Camera Behavior
Smoothed out several other camera behaviors in a variety of situations like mounts, Footplants, drop-ins, kick turns, big airs, rollers, climbing and more.

You can select the pin to open an info panel and place a Waypoint or Fast Travel to the location.

Welcome to the 0.30.1 patch notes!

New Features
Gameplay Improvements
UI Improvements
PC Graphics and Performance Updates
Bug Fixes
New Known Issues for Season 3
Isle of Grom skate.Premium Pass Access
Visit the new Ferry Terminal in Blue Light Beach to take the Wet N’ Mild Taxi Co. boat to and from Isle of Grom. For more details about Isle of Grom, visit our Season 3 article.
Dark Catches and Darkslides

Darkslides and Dark Catches are a fan favorite, returning from previous Skate games with some new improvements. Getting into a Dark Catch is done by holding RB/R1 before or right after performing any flip trick (including Impossible flip tricks from Season 2). Landing into a slide on a rail or ledge while holding a Dark Catch will start a Darkslide, which can now also be leaned and grind adjusted. When exiting, you can Flip Trick out to get some pop with it, or lean exit to ride out smoothly. You'll also find a few new settings to control when and how Dark Catches and Slides are released. Visit Skatepedia for more information about these new tricks.

Developer’s Note: After getting the foundational mechanics into a good place, we're excited to add Darkslides and Dark Catches to skate. Similar to our approach with most legacy mechanics, we wanted to ensure Darkslides and Catches feel familiar, are integrated with other new additions to the franchise—such as flip speed control and grind leans—and have been expanded upon to provide more self expression.
Tasks
Expanded and diversified Tasks, including new varieties that can be completed conveniently while skating.

Developer’s Note: We received feedback that some of the previous Tasks were too difficult or tedious to complete. In response, we’re introducing a wider variety of Tasks designed to complement your skating experience, rather than dominate it.
Party Collision

This feature allows you to collide with others in your party while skating together, adding to the chaos (and fun) of your seshes. Party Collision is disabled by default, but can be enabled in the Settings tab of the Social menu.

Developer’s Note: You may experience collision accuracy and timing discrepancies when using this setting. We hope you enjoy this chaotic, but fun, new way to play with your party, and look forward to your feedback.
Character Customization Options
4 new Hair and 5 Tattoo options have been added to the Character Customizer.
Developer’s Note: 32 ** additional Tattoos can be acquired from Missions, the Skate Paddy’s event, the skate. Pass (Standard and Premium), and the new Essentials Shop.
Skater Presets
You can now configure up to 3 unique Skater Presets, including appearance and clothing. Additional preset slots can be purchased for 250 San Van Bucks. Maximum 10 slots.
Store
Up to 5 Product Boxes can now be bought in a single purchase, making your transactions more streamlined.
An Essentials Shop was added to the Store, with options for Tattoos, Boards and more.
Bonelesses
Improved responsiveness, reliability, and behavior of Boneless tricks performed from the ground or transitions. This change also applies to Fastplants and Bean Plants.

Developer’s Note: We needed to make some large changes to how Bonelesses were originally implemented in order to improve their consistency and quality. A side effect of these underlying changes was the removal of some Boneless-specific “pop glitches.”
Seasonal Missions
Some Missions are now only available for the duration of the season they release in.
Replay Editor
Added an Effects Tab that lets you control Exposure, Color Temperature, Color Saturation, Barrel Distortion, and Vignette (Opacity, Size, Sharpness).
Added more granular volume control over your skater's audio, other skaters’ audio, and world ambience.
Playback speed can now be keyframed as well.
Developer’s Note: Pair the Barrel Distortion effect with a wide Field of View to get that classic Fisheye effect you know and love.
Throwdowns
A notification system to highlight nearby Throwdowns has been added. You can toggle this feature on via the settings and also control the types of Throwdown notifications you see.
Sense of Speed Audio Improvements
Improved passbys and tunnel transitions
Challenge Celebrations
During the celebration screen for Challenges and Throwdowns, your skater’s first equipped Gesture will be played. You can control the Gesture that’s performed by using LB/L1 and the D-pad.
Tasks
Weekly and Monthly Tasks are now grouped in the UI for increased readability.
Player Status
A status communicating whether you’re in an activity, menu, or away has been added to the Social and Spectate menu.
Store
You can now preview items in the Store by hovering over them. We’ve also added a side navigation bar to make browsing the Store more efficient.
Replacing PC benchmark

To give you a better PC performance experience, we're updating how we score users Render GPUs and CPUs based on live data. The new scoring system will slot each card into a more accurate global graphics quality tier. This change could potentially move some players up or down in visual quality, in favor of a better performance experience.
If you’ve been having performance issues, try resetting your graphics settings to default.
Render FPS
Adds an explicit 30/60/uncapped FPS render setting.
"Uncapped" FPS render setting runs at up to 240 FPS
Improves handling of FPS in full-screen mode, particularly when other refresh rates are chosen.
V-Sync
Defaults V-Sync to ON as we believe this will give most players a better experience.
Improves handling of V-Sync in full-screen mode.
Minimum global graphics quality
New global graphics quality introduced that reduces render settings for devices that don't meet our min spec.
Skate PC Min Spec Updates

We’ve analyzed our PC min specs and have updated it to ensure a smoother playing experience. Hardware below the minimum specs can still play but will be placed into the minimum global graphics quality.

[p align="start"]Building skate. with the community means listening, learning, and being transparent about how we balance fixing issues and testing our systems with improving the game and adding new content. Thank you for joining us on this journey. If you haven’t yet, take a look at our Season 2 article to discover the new skateable locations, brands, soundtrack additions, and skate.Pass coming to skate. this season.

[p align="start"]Co-op Mode: Own the Lot

[p align="start"]Own the Lot pushes up to four players to complete as many reqs as possible while racing against the clock. Team up with friends to take on shared challenges of scaling difficulty and own the streets of San Van together, earning Tix in the process.
[p align="start"]Own the Lot also includes special season-long Tasks that grant rewards. For more information about Own the Lot, visit our Season 2 article.

[p align="start"]Developer Note: Own the Lot is tuned for party play. We don’t recommend trying to complete these challenges on your own, and in fact, it will be quite difficult to do as a solo player.
[p align="start"]Flip Tricks
Impossible Flips
Front Foot Impossible Flips
Nollie Impossible Flips
Nollie Back Foot Impossible Flips
All Impossible Flips can also be performed as Held, Late, and from Grinds and Manuals
[p align="start"]Handplant Tricks
14 New Handplant Variants have been added, making for 16 total.
Handplants, including One-Foot, No-Foot, and Tweaked Handplants can also be performed in Fakie stance.
Handplants can now be held for different durations based on how long you hold the input.
Multiple Handplant variants can now be chained back-to-back within the same plant.

[p align="start"]Developer’s Note: When it comes to Flip Tricks, proper Impossibles have been a common request. So, we've not only added new gestures and animations for base Impossible Flips, but also, new variations like Nollies and Front-Foots to give you more options. On the vert skating side, we've also revamped Handplants to feel better, give more control, and fill out all the missing trick variants we didn't get to at Early Access launch. We’re looking forward to seeing these new additions show up in clips, expand your options for lines, and provide more variation for challenges. We are always looking for ways to enhance the experience and give as much control over your skater and experience as possible. Darkslides and more will be coming in future seasons, but until then, we hope you enjoy these updates and look forward to your feedback so we can keep improving the skating experience.
[p align="start"]Challenges

[p align="start"]A bevy of Challenges spread across the Casper Hotel Rooftop, Road Tunnel, Building Roof Patio, and Canal Buildings, and the rest of San Van are powersliding into Season 2. We’ve made big improvements to how we deliver and refresh Seasonal Challenges based on community feedback—Seasonal Challenges will still drop each week, but we’ll also reset them twice over the season, giving you more opportunities to earn Tix.

[p align="start"]Each individual challenge won’t give quite as many Tix, but over the season you’ll be able to earn more than twice the Tix from Seasonal Challenges, not including the Tix you can also earn from the new Own the Lots. Plus, the amount of challenges dropping per week in Season 2 has been increased. For a full breakdown of these changes, including how many more Tix you’ll earn each season, visit our Season 2 article.
[p align="start"]Missions

[p align="start"]Point of Impossibility will bring you underground on a hunt for the place where the Impossible was first landed in San Van. The Mission is unlocked after completion of Shingo's Secret Scoring Tips mission in Tour 2. Completing Point of Impossibility rewards you with 500 Tix and three new Props.

[p align="start"]Coping Inspector will take you to the rooftops for some Handplant practice at a handful of the newly added rooftop spots, and unlocks after completion of The Gift of Grab mission in Tour 3. Completing Coping Inspector rewards you with 500 Tix, the Coping Inspector title, and a Rooftop Fast Travel Point.

Weekly Tasks will last three weeks, giving you time to catch up on any missed Tasks.
Seasonal Tasks are now Monthly Tasks.
Developer’s Note: This change was made to Seasonal Tasks to inject more variety and rewards into your experience.
Auto-claim Task rewards
Now, if you forget to manually claim your Task rewards, they will automatically appear within 24 hours of when the Task ended as a login message.

5 hair, 2 facial hair, and 3 eye shape customization options have been added to the character creator.

Trim replay
Add, edit, and navigate keyframes, interpolating between camera types and camera targets.

[p align="start"]Party Voice Chat
You can now activate Party Voice Chat from the Party Settings, and converse with their party members using a microphone.
Whomever is currently speaking will have their name displayed on screen with the appropriate mic status icons.
You can choose to mute individual party members and not hear their voice audio. This only affects you, not the rest of the party.

Party Up? is now available as a statement in the Communications Wheel. Using this statement drops a beacon in the world that other players can interact with to join your party.
Your beacon is automatically cleared when the party is full or if you join another party.
[p align="start"]skate.Pass

[p align="start"]Developer’s Note: Community conversations have made it clear that you want more ways to play, earn Tix, and express yourself through cosmetics. In Season 1 the skate.pass was designed to help you earn the items you wanted most. But we learned that many of you enjoy the feeling of completing the skate.Pass from start to finish.

[p align="start"]For Season 2, we’re aiming to support both approaches. We’ve tuned the amount of Tix required to unlock rewards pages on the skate.Pass. You will also find we added a bit more SVB for you to collect this time around. We’re also actively considering additional places where Tix can be exchanged outside the skate.Pass, such as at Extravert. All in all, the Season 2 skate.Pass will have tighter scaling to promote quicker progression through the earlier pages of the skate.Pass.

Legacy skate.Pass lets you keep progressing and claiming rewards from the premium pass you bought last season while the new season is live. Only your most recent previous premium skate.pass is eligible. Any progress you make from earning Tix will be applied to both your Season 1 Legacy skate.Pass and your Season 2 skate.Pass.
